evidence.positive: Against the running app (demo-demo tenant) created patient pos-fake-5bdcae0a (case 40025) via the admin API and added an allergy with POST /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/allergies?type=RXNORM&identifier=3355 (diclofenac, an NSAID-group code with no formulary RxNorm mapping in demo). DB then held a patient_medication_allergies row for that patient with medication_category=NSAID and medication=null. As loopuser, POST /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/40025 {medicationIdentifier:"m-ketorolac"} returned results=[a-general-allergy] with details ALLERGY_ALLERGEN="NSAID", ALLERGY_REACTION="Hives", MEDICATION_NAME="Ketorolac", needsAction=true, and the ALLERGIES entry showed isMedicationAllergy=true, medication="NSAID". Repeated with type=SNOMED identifier=372665008 (class-level NSAID code) on patient possn-fake-853f459a: ketorolac again fired a-general-allergy with ALLERGY_ALLERGEN="NSAID". Repeated with RxNorm 5640 (ibuprofen) on posibu-fake-f9c514de: ketorolac fired a-general-allergy, but ALLERGY_ALLERGEN read "Famotidine" (see blockers).
evidence.negative: Same NSAID-allergic patient (pos-fake-5bdcae0a) selecting m-propofol returned results=[] (no a-general-allergy). New patient negb-fake-6e56fdc4 with RxNorm 8782 (propofol, directly mapped, not in any cross-reaction group): DB row was medication=Propofol with no category; selecting m-ketorolac returned results=[] while selecting m-propofol fired a-general-allergy with ALLERGY_ALLERGEN="Propofol" (existing direct-mapping path intact, group path not over-applied). New patient negc-fake-135ae38b with unknown RxNorm 999999: no patient_medication_allergies row created and m-ketorolac returned results=[].
evidence.red_check: Data flip: deleted rxnorm_code 3355 from demo-demo.allergy_cross_reaction_group_rxnorm_codes for the NSAID group (count of 3355 rows went 1 -> 0). Staged a fresh patient redflip-fake-9aca3ded (case 77379) with the same RXNORM 3355 allergy: DB created no patient_medication_allergies row for it, and m-ketorolac selection returned results=[] with no a-general-allergy, i.e. the positive check went red. The RuleEngine "Rule context" DEBUG line for that selection shows medicationAllergies=[] alongside the 3355 ContextAllergy. Reverted by re-inserting the 3355 row (count back to 1, NSAID group back to 53 codes), then staged postrevert-fake-a830539c: DB row medication_category=NSAID reappeared and m-ketorolac fired a-general-allergy with ALLERGY_ALLERGEN="NSAID" again. The pre-fix class swap was not attempted; the data flip exercised the exact clause (group membership) the ticket adds.

blockers: In demo and mgb master-rxnorm-list.csv, RxNorm 5640 (ibuprofen) maps to g-famotidine, m-famotidine-oral, m-gabapentin and m-omeprazole, and 7258 (naproxen) maps to m-esomeprazole (mayo maps 5640 to ibuprofen correctly). Observed at runtime: an ibuprofen allergy in demo created medication allergies to Famotidine, Famotidine Oral, Gabapentin and Omeprazole, and the ketorolac NSAID alert labelled the allergen "Famotidine". Are those crosswalk rows (PR #4476) intentional, or must they be removed before the NSAID group is considered done?

Given the above, should the NSAID cross-reaction alert label prefer the group/category name over the first RxNorm-mapped medication name when the match came through the category (today MedicationAllergyRule.resolveAllergenName prefers the medication mapping, by design per its unit test)?
caveats: RXNORM_ALLERGY_MAPPING is disabled for every tenant (enabledTenants []); the real FHIR ingestion path (Mayo/MGB GetPatientInfo strategies) is gated on it, so nothing changes in production until the flag is turned on. The admin RXNORM/SNOMED allergy endpoint bypasses the flag and was the surface used here.
Real FHIR AllergyIntolerance ingestion was not exercised; the admin endpoint calls the same associateAllergiesViaRxNormMapping the strategies call.
Only the demo-demo tenant and the single-component m-ketorolac were exercised; multi-component NSAID combos (RECK) and the SULFONAMIDE group were not.
Pre-fix class swap red check was not attempted; the data flip on the group membership table was used instead.
The wrong "Famotidine" label and spurious famotidine/gabapentin/omeprazole allergies for an ibuprofen-coded allergy affect demo and mgb data only; mayo data is correct.

automation.assessment: Backend unit coverage is solid: AllergyAssociationServiceTest covers RxNorm and SNOMED group matches, dedupe and the flag; MedicationAllergyRuleTest covers category match, abstain, and name resolution; AllergyCrossReactionGroupRepositoryTest covers the query. qa-suite has only ALG-001 (cefazolin/penicillin) and no RxNorm/SNOMED coded-allergy scenario, and nothing guards the crosswalk data against mapping an NSAID ingredient code to a non-NSAID medication, which is the defect found here.
proposed_tests: ALG supplemental (API-only, patient-api fixture): RXNORM 3355 allergy then medication-selection m-ketorolac asserts a-general-allergy with details.ALLERGY_ALLERGEN === NSAID, paired with the same patient selecting m-propofol asserting no a-general-allergy.
ALG supplemental: SNOMED 372665008 allergy then m-ketorolac asserts a-general-allergy with ALLERGY_ALLERGEN NSAID.
ALG supplemental negative: RXNORM 8782 (propofol) allergy then m-ketorolac asserts no a-general-allergy while m-propofol asserts ALLERGY_ALLERGEN Propofol.

Backend data-integrity test over each org master-rxnorm-list.csv: every RxNorm code listed in allergy-cross-reaction-groups.csv for the NSAID group must map only to medications carrying the NSAID category (would fail today on demo/mgb 5640 -> famotidine/gabapentin/omeprazole and 7258 -> esomeprazole).

jira_comment:
Verdict: not-deploy-ready.

Positive: A diclofenac RxNorm allergy and a SNOMED NSAID class allergy each produced an NSAID category medication allergy and ketorolac selection fired the general allergy alert labelled NSAID.
Negative: The same patient selecting propofol, a propofol RxNorm allergy selecting ketorolac, and an unknown RxNorm code all produced no NSAID alert.
Red check: Removing diclofenac from the NSAID group table made the ketorolac alert disappear for a fresh patient, and restoring the row brought it back.

Blocker: In demo and mgb the RxNorm crosswalk maps ibuprofen 5640 to famotidine, gabapentin and omeprazole, so an ibuprofen allergy creates allergies to those drugs and the ketorolac alert reads Famotidine.

Automation: Proposed API-only ALG supplemental tests for the RxNorm, SNOMED and negative cases plus a data test that NSAID group codes map only to NSAID medications.
